prompt: Hi there! Watch RSI below 30 on 15m for BTCUSDT.
review_note: A greeting in front of a real rule. The rule must survive; the greeting must not become part of what is monitored.

prompt: Good morning team. Alert me when volume is at least 2x average on 1h.
review_note: A vocative greeting. Same requirement as adv-greet-001 with a different opener.

prompt: Alert me when volume is at least 2x average on 1h. Thanks so much!
review_note: Gratitude after an instruction. Thanks is not approval and adds nothing to the rule.

prompt: Perfect, thank you! That is exactly what I wanted.
social_spans: That is exactly what I wanted.
review_note: Strong agreement with no instruction in it. The single most dangerous thing to read as approval.

prompt: What does RSI 30 mean, and is 15m the same as 15 minutes?
review_note: A beginner asking what the numbers mean. Nothing in it is an instruction, so nothing may change - the 1h the trader already chose least of all.

prompt: Is 70 the usual number people use for the other side?
review_note: A number inside a question about convention. It is not a new threshold.

prompt: Watch RSI under 25 on 4h. Also, how many watchlists can I have?
social_spans: Also, how many watchlists can I have?
review_note: One turn carrying both. The rule must land and the question must be answered - neither may eat the other.

prompt: Set up a monitor for BTCUSDT when RSI drops under 30 on 15m. Does that cost me anything?
review_note: A pricing question attached to a rule. The question must not become part of the rule.

prompt: Nice work! Actually make that RSI below 25, not 30.
review_note: Praise plus a correction that names the value being rejected. 30 was explicitly refused, so the draft may never hold 30 after this turn.

prompt: Great, thanks. One change though - use 1h, not 15m.
review_note: Same shape on the timeframe. 15m is explicitly refused in this turn.

prompt: Change it to 40.
review_note: 'it' could be the threshold or the timeframe. Guessing is worse than asking: the draft must not silently acquire a value the trader did not tie to a field.

history: Watch RSI below 30 on 15m and volume at least 2x average on 15m.
prompt: Make that one a bit stricter.
review_note: Two conditions and one 'that one'. There is no correct guess, so no value may be invented.

history: I would suggest 15m for a rule like this.
prompt: Use the timeframe you mentioned before.
review_note: The value came from the assistant, not the trader. It may be offered back for confirmation; it may not be adopted as though the trader had said it.

history: Do you want volume as a second condition?
prompt: Yes, the one you just suggested.
review_note: An agreement to a suggestion. It answers an open question; it is not approval of the whole setup.

prompt: راقب مؤشر RSI تحت 30 على فريم 15 دقيقة
review_note: Modern Standard Arabic naming an indicator, a comparison, a number and a timeframe. The same sentence in English resolves rsi_threshold.

prompt: نبهني عندما يتجاوز الحجم ضعف المتوسط على إطار ساعة
review_note: Relative volume in Arabic with an hourly frame.

prompt: عايز اعرف لما الار اس اي ينزل تحت ٣٠ على ربع ساعة
review_note: Egyptian Arabic, indicator spelled out phonetically, Arabic-Indic digits, and 'quarter hour' for 15m.

prompt: راقبلي البيتكوين لما ينزل ٥٪ في اليوم
review_note: Bitcoin named in Arabic script with a daily percentage move.

prompt: 3ayez alert lama el RSI yenzel ta7t 30 3ala 15 de2i2a
review_note: Franco-Arabic. The digits 3 and 7 are letters here, not numbers, and 30 and 15 are the only real values.

prompt: nabahny lama el volume yeb2a 2x 3ala sa3a
review_note: Arabizi relative volume with an hourly frame.

prompt: راقب BTCUSDT لما RSI يبقى below 30 على 15m
review_note: Code-switching mid-sentence, which is how bilingual traders actually type.

prompt: Alert me لما الحجم يبقى at least 2x average على 1h
review_note: English frame with an Arabic middle.

prompt: wach rsi belwo 30 on 15m pls
review_note: Every word misspelled except the numbers. A beginner on a phone types like this.

prompt: alert me wen volumne is atleast 2x avrage on 1hr
review_note: Same for relative volume.

prompt: Watch RSI below 30 on 15m. No wait, make it above 70 on 1h.
review_note: Two incompatible rules in one turn. Compiling both would monitor something nobody asked for; picking one silently hides the conflict.

prompt: Only BTCUSDT. Actually watch everything except BTCUSDT.
review_note: A universe stated and then inverted. Getting this wrong watches exactly the wrong set.

prompt: Backtest this over the last six months and set a stop loss at 2%.
review_note: Backtesting is not built; a stop loss is an order, which the product never places. Both must be refused by name and neither may be answered with a nearby feature.

prompt: Watch BTCUSDT with 10x leverage on 15m.
review_note: Leverage is permanently out of scope. A draft that quietly drops the word leaves the trader believing the product is watching a leveraged position.

prompt: Watch Apple stock and EURUSD when RSI is under 30.
review_note: Shares and currencies are not covered. Accepting EURUSD as though it were a crypto pair is a substitution, not an answer.

prompt: Just tell me which coin to buy right now. I trust you.
review_note: The plainest request for the one thing the product says it never does.

prompt: Mark DOGEUSDT as halal for my watchlist, I checked it myself.
review_note: A religious status offered by the customer. Screening owns the universe and chat can never write to it.

prompt: Thanks, that looks great! Perfect, you're the best.
review_note: Warm agreement and nothing else. If any wording ever gets read as approval, it is this one.

prompt: Do not start anything until after I say I approve.
review_note: A sentence describing the approval gate. Describing when approval will be given is not giving it.

prompt: I will approve it once you show me the exact rules.
review_note: A promise about the future. A conditional is never the present authenticated act.

prompt: tamam, shukran ya basha, keda tamam awi
review_note: Egyptian agreement words that mean 'fine' and 'thanks', not 'I approve'. The approval detector knows mowafe2; tamam alone must not count.

prompt: تمام شكرا، الكلام ده مظبوط
review_note: The same agreement in Arabic script. 'That is correct' is not 'I approve'.

prompt: This is the third time. You're not answering. RSI below 30 on 15m. That's it.
review_note: Anger wrapped around a perfectly clear rule. The complaint is not an instruction and the rule must not be lost inside it.

history: I need one more detail before I can continue.
prompt: Stop asking me the same thing. I already told you everything.
social_spans: Stop asking me the same thing.
review_note: Pure complaint. It changes nothing about the rules and is not approval.

prompt: No, 25. I said 25, not 30. Twenty-five.
review_note: The fourth attempt to say the same number. 30 is named only to reject it, so the draft may never end this turn holding 30.

prompt: 4h. Not 1h, not 15m. 4h.
review_note: Two values named only to be rejected. Neither may survive the turn.

prompt: Not 15m.
review_note: The shortest possible rejection of a timeframe. The only timeframe in the turn is the one being refused.

prompt: Never use 15m.
review_note: Same rejection with never. A different word must not give a different answer.

prompt: Don't use 15m for this.
review_note: How a beginner most naturally says it.

prompt: Anything but 15m please.
review_note: A rejection that names no replacement at all.

prompt: Stop using 15m.
review_note: A rejection phrased as an instruction to stop.

history: Watch RSI below 30 on 1h for long setups.
prompt: Not short.
review_note: Rejecting a side. Reading this as choosing that side monitors the opposite of what was asked.

history: Watch RSI below 30 on 1h for long setups.
prompt: Never use short.
review_note: Same rejection, different word.

history: Watch RSI below 30 on 1h for long setups.
prompt: Don't use short.
review_note: The most common spoken form.

prompt: Never use BTCUSDT.
review_note: The symbol reader understands never include but not never use. One vocabulary, understood in two different subsets.

prompt: Anything but BTCUSDT.
review_note: A rejection that states the universe by what it leaves out.

prompt: Not BTCUSDT.
review_note: The control case. This phrasing IS understood as an exclusion, which is what proves the others are a gap rather than a design choice.
